key_idea: Classic deadline scheduling: process stores by increasing deadline h, keep adding, and whenever total time exceeds the current deadline drop the longest job taken so far.
sketch: Sort by h. Maintain a max-heap of chosen round-trip times and their sum; push each store, and if the sum exceeds its h, pop the largest t. The heap size at the end is the answer. O(n log n). The exchange argument: dropping the longest job keeps the count and minimizes the elapsed time for every prefix. Pitfalls: sums reach 2e14 so use 64-bit, and finishing exactly at time h is allowed (sum <= h), which the samples confirm.
